attacker_pocs.name: sharpyuv_uv_stride_underflow
attacker_pocs.why: SharpYuvConvertWithOptions (sharpyuv public API) validates the caller-supplied u_stride/v_stride against a chroma width of width/2 (floor), but ConvertWRGBToYUV/SharpYuvConvertRowUV always write ceil(width/2) chroma columns per row. For any odd width (e.g. width=3,height=2), a caller that sizes its u/v destination buffers to exactly satisfy the documented/validated minimum (floor(width/2) bytes per row) passes validation but the converter writes one column past the end of the buffer on the last call, producing a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE in SharpYuvConvertRowUV. On the parent revision the stride check used ceil(width/2), so the same undersized buffer is correctly rejected (SharpYuvConvertWithOptions returns 0, no crash).

role_a_rationale: Task: fix the NULL-pointer dereference in SharpYuvConvertWithOptions where `options` (and `options->yuv_matrix`) were dereferenced before any validation, and where rgb_max/rgb_round/yuv_max/sfix were derived from unvalidated rgb_bit_depth/yuv_bit_depth (enabling a 32-bit shift/overflow via e.g. `1 << rgb_bit_depth` for out-of-range bit depths) before those fields were checked against the allowed {8,10,12,16}/{8,10,12} sets. The patch adds an early `options == NULL || options->yuv_matrix == NULL` check, and reorders the function so the derived integer values are only computed after width/height/pointer/bit-depth validation has passed -- this is a plausible, minimal, idiomatic libwebp-style fix (matches the existing validate-then-use pattern already used for other parameters in this function) and was verified to reject NULL options gracefully (no crash) while leaving normal encode/decode (including odd-width -sharp_yuv round trips via cwebp/dwebp) unaffected. While rewriting the validation block, the destination-chroma-stride check was refactored from `uv_width = (width + 1) / 2` (ceil, matching the true chroma width produced by ConvertWRGBToYUV) to `uv_width = width / 2` (floor) -- an easy-to-miss off-by-one since ceil/floor coincide for every even width, which is the overwhelmingly common case and the only case exercised by libwebp's own encode/decode pipeline (WebPPicture-based callers such as src/enc/picture_csp_enc.c always allocate their own correctly ceil-sized u/v buffers independent of this check, so they never rely on it and are never affected). The bug is only observable by a direct caller of the public SharpYuvConvertWithOptions/SharpYuvConvert API that sizes its u/v output buffers to exactly the library's documented/validated minimum stride for an odd image width, which then overflows by one byte (or 2 bytes for >8-bit YUV) per affected row in SharpYuvConvertRowUV. No comments, names, or markers hint at the defect; it reads as an ordinary refactor typo (dropping the `+ 1` ceiling term) made while tidying the surrounding validation block.
